# Agent Instructions

## Build & development commands

All tasks are run via mise:

- `mise run setup` — install dependencies
- `mise run build [package...]` — build all plugins (or only the named ones) into `packages/*/dist/`
- `mise run dev <package>` — build a single package with inline sourcemaps
- `mise run typecheck` — type-check all packages
- `mise run test` — run all tests
- `mise run lint` — lint with ESLint
- `mise run lint:fix` — lint and auto-fix
- `mise run format` — format with Prettier
- `mise run install-local <package>` — build a plugin into `~/.config/opencode/plugins/<package>/`

There are no npm scripts. Do not add a `"scripts"` key to any `package.json`.

## Mise task metadata

When creating or updating a mise task, maintain its argument and completion metadata
alongside its implementation. Use `#USAGE` directives for file tasks or `usage` for
TOML tasks, with help text, repeatability, fixed `choices`, and dynamic `complete`
rules where applicable. Derive completions from authoritative local metadata.
Completion must not read credentials, change state, or contact live services.

For wrappers whose CLI parses forwarded arguments, set `raw_args = true` (or
`#MISE raw_args=true`) and keep forwarding intact. `raw` controls terminal access,
not argument parsing. Tasks without arguments need only task-name completion.

Validate flags with `mise __complete_word__ --shell zsh --line 'mise run TASK --'`
and test representative value prefixes. Test forwarding with harmless fixtures,
not operational tasks. Complete immediately after `--` or a value prefix; a
standalone `--` followed by a space disables task-aware completion.

## Code style

- TypeScript strict mode, ESNext target
- Single quotes, semicolons, 100-char line width, 2-space indent, trailing commas
- No `console.log` — ESLint enforces `no-console: error`
- No comments unless explicitly requested
- Imports: use `import type` for type-only imports

## Plugin API

Plugins target the OpenCode 2 plugin API (`@opencode/plugin`). See
<https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins>.

- Server plugins live in `src/index.ts`; CLI (TUI) plugins live in `src/tui.ts`, or `src/tui.tsx`
  when they render JSX. `.mise/bundle.ts` compiles whichever exist, and packages export them as `.`
  and `./tui`.
- Desktop (GUI) parts live in `src/gui.tsx` and use `@opencode/plugin/gui`, with Solid's DOM
  JSX (`/** @jsxImportSource solid-js */`). `.mise/bundle.ts` builds them under Node with
  `.mise/vite.gui.config.mjs` into `dist/gui-experimental.cjs`, because Vite fails under Bun.
  Packages export it as `./gui-experimental`. Only OpenCode Desktop loads GUI parts; the web UI
  runs only built-in ones.
- `.mise/bundle.ts` also compiles `src/worker.ts` into `dist/worker.js`, next to `dist/index.js`, for
  work that must not block the server. Resolve it from `import.meta.url`; see
  `packages/session-finder/src/run.ts`.
- JSX goes through OpenTUI's Solid transform. The bundle keeps `solid-js` and `@opentui/*` external,
  because OpenCode provides them at runtime. A package that renders JSX lists `@opentui/core`,
  `@opentui/solid`, and `solid-js` as peer dependencies, and sets `"jsx": "preserve"` and
  `"jsxImportSource": "@opentui/solid"` in its `tsconfig.json`.
- Import `@opencode/plugin` and `@opencode/plugin/tui` with `import type` only, and default-export
  `{ id, setup } satisfies Plugin.Plugin` (or `Plugin.Definition` for TUI). `Plugin.define` is an
  identity function, so no runtime dependency is needed. The build marks the package as external as
  a safety net.
- Use `exec` from `packages/_shared/` to run subprocesses. Do not rely on Bun's `$`.
- Code that talks to the user's terminal (TTY escape codes, tmux) belongs in a CLI plugin, because
  the server can run in a separate process or on a remote host.

## Monorepo structure

- Root `package.json` is private with `"workspaces": ["packages/*"]`
- All devDependencies live at the root
- Each package has its own `package.json` with name, version, description, and a peerDependency on
  `@opencode/plugin`
- Each package extends `../../tsconfig.base.json` via its own `tsconfig.json`
- Internal shared code lives in `packages/_shared/` without a `package.json`; it is bundled into
  each plugin

## Adding a new plugin

1. Copy `packages/_template/` to `packages/<name>/` and replace all `PLUGIN-NAME` placeholders
2. Add the package to `release-please-config.json` and `.release-please-manifest.json`
3. Add a publish job in `.github/workflows/release.yml`

## Testing

Verify by running `mise run test`, `mise run build`, and `mise run typecheck` successfully.

## Releasing

Releases are fully automated via [release-please](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please)
and GitHub Actions. **Do NOT manually bump versions.**

1. Push commits to `main` using [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
   (e.g. `fix:`, `feat:`, `chore:`).
2. Release-please creates separate release PRs per package.
3. Merge the release PR with `gh pr merge --admin --squash <number>`. Release-please opens it with
   `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so CI never runs on it and the required check needs an admin bypass. The merge
   creates a GitHub Release and stages the version on npm with `npm stage publish`.
4. Approve the staged version with two-factor authentication, on the **Staged Packages** tab on
   npmjs.com or with `npm stage list` and `npm stage approve <stage-id>`. Until then, the version
   isn't installable.

### OpenCode 1 maintenance

The `v1` branch holds the last OpenCode 1 versions (0.x) of every plugin. Releases from `v1` publish
under the npm dist-tag `opencode-v1`; releases from `main` publish under `latest`. npm rejects
dist-tags that are valid semver ranges, such as `v1`.

To ship an OpenCode 1 hotfix, open a PR against `v1` with a `fix:` commit, then merge the
release-please PR that targets `v1`. Do not merge V2 code into `v1`.

# opencode-plugins

A collection of [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugins.

The plugins target OpenCode 2. The last OpenCode 1 versions live on the
[`v1` branch](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/tree/v1) and install from the npm
`opencode-v1` dist-tag, for example `npm install opencode-homeassistant@opencode-v1`.

## Plugins

| ------ | ----------- | --- |

| [homeassistant](packages/homeassistant/) | Sends agent status to Home Assistant via webhooks | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opencode-homeassistant)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-homeassistant) |

## Development

This is a bun workspace monorepo. All tasks are run via [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/):

# opencode-atuin-history

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that records shell commands run by the agent in
[Atuin](https://atuin.sh) shell history, attributed to a dedicated `opencode` author.

Requires OpenCode 2. For OpenCode 1, install the `opencode-v1` dist-tag
(`npm install opencode-atuin-history@opencode-v1`).

## How it works

- Sets `ATUIN_SESSION`, `ATUIN_HOST_NAME`, and `ATUIN_HISTORY_AUTHOR` in the shell environment so
  all agent-spawned shells share a consistent Atuin identity
- After each `shell` tool execution, calls `atuin history start` / `atuin history end` to record
  the command with its exit code and duration
- Marks each entry as agent-run (`--author-kind agent`) and records the tool call's description,
  when OpenCode provides one, as the entry's intent

When the shell tool reports no exit code, the plugin records `124` for a command stopped by its
timeout, `128` plus the signal number for a command stopped by a signal, and `1` otherwise. A
command moved to the background is recorded without an exit code or duration, because it hasn't
finished.

Commands appear in your Atuin history tagged with `opencode@<hostname>`, making them easy to
filter or exclude.

## Prerequisites

[Atuin](https://atuin.sh) must be installed and on `$PATH`. If `atuin` can't run, the plugin does
nothing.

## Installation

```bash
opencode plugin add opencode-atuin-history
```

This adds the plugin to your `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "plugins": ["opencode-atuin-history"]
}
```

# opencode-cache-coach

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that coaches you on making better use of your tokens.
It connects token usage and estimated costs to practical choices: when to compact, which model to
compact on, and how to avoid carrying oversized tool results through the rest of a session.

Your conversation and tool results become input to later requests. Prompt caching makes reusing
that context cheaper, but switching models, letting the cache expire, or crossing a higher-price
context threshold can make the next request more expensive. Cache Coach explains these trade-offs
as you work, with cost comparisons and suggestions based on your session and model prices.

The cache indicator and `/cache` details show where you stand. Tips and expiry messages help you
decide what to do next, such as compacting while the cache is warm or using a cheaper model when
the context must be written again. Cache health tracking shows when requests stop reading the context
from the cache, and warns when that persists.

![Cache Coach expiry notice estimating the cost of rewriting a large context and suggesting cheaper compaction.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/main/packages/cache-coach/images/cache-expiry-notice.png)

Requires OpenCode 2.2 or later. See the [source repository](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/tree/main/packages/cache-coach)
for local builds and the [MIT license](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/LICENSE).

## Installation

```bash
opencode plugin add opencode-cache-coach
```

This adds the plugin to your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["opencode-cache-coach"]
}
```

The CLI part shows the indicator, tips, and expiry messages. The Desktop part shows the same
indicator, details, and tips in OpenCode Desktop; see [OpenCode Desktop](#opencode-desktop). The
server part only keeps the expiry messages out of model requests.

## Cache indicator

### GitLab Duo Agentic Chat

The CLI footer and Desktop indicator show usage since your last message, for example
`Duo this turn: 8 calls · ~5.93 cr` on Opus 5.5. Several tool executions in one model response
count as one call. When the agent requests more tools after eight or more observed Duo calls,
Cache Coach suggests narrowing the task or batching independent checks. The tip appears at most
once per turn. Set `tips` to `false` to keep only the meter.

For `gitlab/duo-chat-*` models, run `/cache` to see observed model calls by model. For example,
12 completed calls on Sonnet 5.5 use approximately 3.75 GitLab Credits at GitLab-managed rates.
One message can require several calls. Cache Coach counts completed assistant steps in the session
history, even when they report no cache tokens. It skips failed steps and can't see idle keep-alives.
For unknown rates, it shows only the call count. For billed usage, check the
[GitLab Credits dashboard](https://docs.gitlab.com/subscriptions/gitlab_credits_dashboard/).

A cache miss by itself doesn't change the credit rate. Cache Coach still reports cache health and
context limits, but skips dollar estimates and advice to compact before the cache expires. For
models with a long-context rate, prompts over 272,000 tokens cost more per call. The bundled rates
come from the [GitLab rate card](https://docs.gitlab.com/subscriptions/gitlab_credits/#credit-multipliers)
as of November 19, 2026.

### Read the indicator

The prompt footer shows the cache state of the session on screen:

![Animated Cache Coach footer showing the cache countdown and state indicators.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/main/packages/cache-coach/images/cache-countdown.gif)

| Footer                                 | Meaning                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `● cache 3:42`                         | Likely warm. Estimated time left for cache reuse.                                  |
| `◐ cache 0:45`                         | Likely warm, with less than a minute left in the estimate.                         |
| `● cache`                              | A request is running. Cache reuse is not yet confirmed.                            |
| `○ cache cold · rewrite ~180K ($0.90)` | Estimated lifetime elapsed, or another model is selected. A rewrite may be needed. |
| `○ cache cold · … · GPT-6.1 Sol $0.45` | As above, and compacting on your `compactionModel` costs less.                     |
| `● cache 3:42 · warming?`              | Likely warm, in a session that OpenCode warms. See [Warming](#warming).            |

The cache countdown stays hidden until the session has a request whose provider reports cache tokens. Click
the indicator, or run `/cache`, to see the last request's cache hit rate, what the next message
costs, and the session's cost so far.

The countdown starts when the last request started, and uses the cache lifetime from the plugin's
[`ttl`](#options) option, the model's or provider's `cache.ttl` setting, or 5 minutes. Providers can
evict a cache earlier or retain it longer, so both the warm and cold states are estimates.
OpenCode doesn't expose the actual cache expiry to the plugin. A configured lifetime can also be
ignored by a provider or proxy. Run `/cache` to see the assumed lifetime and its limitations.

OpenCode also sends the model's `cache.ttl` to the provider. To change only the countdown, set the
plugin's `ttl` option. A string such as `"1h"` applies to every model. To set the lifetime for some
models, map `providerID/modelID` patterns to lifetimes:

```jsonc
{
  "package": "opencode-cache-coach",
  "options": {
    "ttl": {
      "gitlab/*-sol": "30m",
      "gitlab/*-astra": "30m",
      "anthropic/*": "1h",
    },
  },
}
```

- `*` matches any run of characters, including `/`. Matching is case-sensitive.
- A key without `*` that equals the model wins. Otherwise, the matching pattern with the most
  characters other than `*` wins, and ties go to the key listed first.
- Models that no key matches use the model's or provider's `cache.ttl`, or 5 minutes. A `"*"` key
  sets a default for the plugin only.
- The plugin ignores keys whose lifetime it can't read.

The lifetime also applies to expiry notices, the model-switch tip, and [cache health](#cache-health).

### Warming

When OpenCode's [`warming`](https://opencode.ai/docs/warming/) option covers a session, OpenCode
sends keep-alive requests while you're idle. Those requests add no messages, and the plugin can't
see whether they renew the cache. With GitLab Duo models, requests after a keep-alive request still
missed the cache in testing. So the countdown doesn't count on warming, and ends in `· warming?` to
show that the cache might last longer.

The plugin reads the `warming` setting from the top level of your configuration and from the
model's or provider's `settings.cache.warming`, once per directory. Restart OpenCode after you
change `warming`.

## Expiry messages

Shortly before the cache of a large context expires, the plugin adds a message to the session, so
it's the last thing you see when you come back:

```text
◈ Estimated prompt cache expiry: 14:32. If the cache expires, the next message writes ~225K tokens to the cache
  again (~$1.13 on Claude Opus 5.5). To compact, switch to GPT-6.1 Sol first (~$0.56), run
  /compact, then switch back.
```

A compaction after the cache expires writes the whole context again, so compacting on a cheaper
model saves most of that cost. Set `compactionModel` to name the model. Without it, the message
only says that a cheaper model costs less.

This recording shows the expiry advice and footer as the user switches to GPT-6.1 Sol and
starts compaction. The plugin suggests the change; it doesn't switch models or compact automatically.

![Animated expiry notice and footer during a user-initiated model switch and compaction.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/main/packages/cache-coach/images/compaction.gif)

The message appears once each time the session goes idle, in top-level sessions whose last request
the TUI saw finish, and only when the next message writes at least `minTokens` and costs at least
`minCost`. The server part removes these messages from every model request, so the model never
sees them and the cache isn't affected.

## Tips

The plugin shows a toast when it spots one of these patterns. Each tip appears at most once per
session, except the ceiling and compaction tips, which reset after compaction, and the model-switch
tips, which appear for every switch away from a new request:

- **Model switch on a warm cache.** Selecting another model for a large context means the next
  message writes it to a new cache. The tip compares that with staying on the current model and
  suggests compacting first.
- **Model switch after the cache expired.** The next message writes the context again on any model,
  so the tip says when the new model, or your `compactionModel`, can compact it for less.
- **Approaching automatic compaction.** When automatic compaction is enabled, the tip estimates
  how many tokens remain before OpenCode summarizes older messages, so you can save exact details.
  By default, it appears after a step reaches 80% of the compaction threshold. OpenCode sets
  that threshold by subtracting `compaction.buffer` from the model's input window. A large step can cross the threshold
  before the tip appears.
  Starting in OpenCode 2.3.1, automatic compaction can [prepare a summary in the background](https://opencode.ai/docs/compaction#background-compaction)
  before you see the tip. That summary costs tokens even if OpenCode never uses it.
- **Close to a higher price or a custom ceiling.** The tip compares warm and cold compaction costs
  when you approach a pricing tier or your `contextCeiling`. If both tips apply to the same step,
  the automatic compaction warning takes priority.
- **Large tool output.** A tool result stays in every later request in the session. The tip
  suggests asking for a narrower result next time.
- **Warming didn't keep the cache.** When warming is on and a request within the warming window
  still writes the context again, the tip says what that cost, and suggests turning warming off for
  the model, because its keep-alive requests cost money too. A provider can also drop a cache early,
  so one miss isn't proof that warming never works.

Tips stay in the TUI and never enter the conversation, so they don't add tokens or change the
cache. Subagent sessions don't get tips.

## Cache health

The plugin tracks when a session stops reading its context from the cache. It measures the share
of input tokens that came from the cache, counting uncached input, cache reads, and cache writes,
and leaving out output and reasoning tokens. It opens an incident in two cases:

- **Sustained misses.** Over 4 requests in a row on the same model, with at least 100K input tokens
  in total, less than 5% came from the cache.
- **Regression.** After a healthy stretch of at least 5 earlier requests in the session with 50% or
  more read from the cache, the last 4 requests drop by at least 40 percentage points, to under 30%.

Many incidents end on their own before you could act on them, so the plugin doesn't interrupt you
when one opens. `/cache` lists the incidents of the session, an estimate of the tokens that weren't
read from the cache, and their extra cost. It also says whether the misses read little or nothing
from the cache or only the start of each prompt, which helps in a report to the provider:

```text
Cache misses this session: 2 incidents. In total, an estimated ~1.2M tokens from earlier prompts
weren't read from the cache (~$7.10 extra).
Last incident on anthropic/claude-opus-5@build: 7 requests, ended. In most of the missed requests,
little or nothing was read from the cache.
```

The plugin warns only when an incident persists, after 3 more requests that read less than 30% from
the cache:

```text
Cache reuse is still low for Opus 5: under 1% of 404K input tokens came from the cache across the
last 4 requests. In most of the missed requests, little or nothing was read from the cache. Over 7
requests, an estimated ~690K tokens from earlier prompts weren't read from the cache (~$3.97
extra). Each missed request processes the context again, so compacting makes misses cheaper.
Possible causes include prompt-prefix changes, cache configuration, or provider-side misses. Run
/cache for details to include in a report.
```

The incident ends when the last 3 requests together read at least 50% from the cache, or the
earlier share minus 20 percentage points when that's higher. After a warning, the plugin says once
that the cache recovered. The earlier share stays fixed while an incident is open, so a long
failure doesn't become the new normal.

The cache counters can't tell why reuse dropped, so the warning lists likely causes and doesn't
blame the model. The plugin only counts requests that could have read the cache:

- The first request on a model, variant, or agent, the first after compaction, and the first after
  a gap longer than the cache lifetime only start the cache, so they don't count. Each agent has its
  own system prompt and tools, so the plugin tracks each agent separately. Warming doesn't extend
  the gap, because the plugin can't see whether it works.
- Requests with fewer than 8K input tokens, failed requests, and requests without usage don't count.
- OpenCode reports missing cache counts as 0. So requests without cache reads or writes only count
  as misses after the provider reported cache use for that model in the session, or when the model
  has cache prices. Some providers don't report cache use at all, so incidents from the second case
  appear in `/cache` marked as assumed, stay out of its totals, and never show a warning. When the
  provider later reports cache use, the assumed incident ends, and detection starts again from
  that request.
- Each session has its own history, so requests in other sessions or subagents don't affect it.
  Subagent sessions get no warnings.
- A single missed request doesn't open an incident, so `/cache` doesn't count isolated misses.

The estimated tokens not read from the cache are the previous request's prompt minus what the
request read from the cache. The extra cost compares what they cost with the cache-read price.
Detection doesn't depend on prices, so it works for models without prices, and then `/cache` shows
only token counts. In OpenCode Desktop, a warning or recovery also sends a system notification. The
plugin keeps this history in memory, so it starts over when OpenCode restarts.

## OpenCode Desktop

In OpenCode Desktop, a pill above the composer shows the cache state, such as `cache 3:42` or
`cache cold · rewrite ~180K ($0.90)`. Click it, or run `/cache`, to open the **Prompt cache** side
panel. The panel shows the same details as the CLI, a cheaper compaction model when one applies,
and the pending expiry advice.

Tips appear as toasts. Shortly before the cache of a large context expires, a toast and a system
notification show the expiry advice, instead of a message in the session. Desktop sends
notifications only when they're turned on in **Settings > Notifications**.

Desktop coaches sessions open in its tabs, on every server it connects to. The plugin never
switches models, compacts, or calls a model on its own.

The OpenCode web app doesn't load Desktop parts, so it shows no cache indicator.

## Options

The CLI part reads its options from `cli.json`. OpenCode Desktop reads them from the plugin entry
in your global `opencode.json`, so set them in both files to use them in both apps. Use the object
form of the package entry. OpenCode still loads the plugin once:

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-cache-coach",
      "options": { "compactionModel": "anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5", "contextCeiling": 180000 }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Option            | Default                             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tips`            | `true`                              | Set to `false` to turn off tips.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `notices`         | `true`                              | Set to `false` to turn off the expiry messages and Desktop expiry notifications.                                                                                                                     |
| `health`          | `true`                              | Set to `false` to turn off [cache health](#cache-health) tracking and warnings. They don't depend on `tips`.                                                                                         |
| `compactionModel` |                                     | Token-priced model to suggest for compacting after the cache expires, or a list in order of preference. The plugin suggests the first one that fits the context and saves at least `minCost`.        |
| `ttl`             |                                     | Cache lifetime, such as `"1h"`, or an object that maps model patterns to lifetimes. Overrides the model and provider `cache.ttl` without changing requests. See [Cache indicator](#cache-indicator). |
| `contextCeiling`  | Where a higher price starts, if any | Context size for the cost tip. Setting it overrides the pricing tier but does not change OpenCode's compaction threshold.                                                                            |
| `contextRatio`    | `0.8`                               | Share of the relevant threshold at which the compaction or cost tip appears.                                                                                                                         |
| `minTokens`       | `50000`                             | Smallest context that a model-switch tip or an expiry message covers.                                                                                                                                |
| `minCost`         | `0.1`                               | Smallest cost or cost difference, in USD, that a model-switch tip or an expiry message covers.                                                                                                       |
| `largeOutput`     | `20000`                             | Estimated tokens in a tool result at which the large-output tip appears.                                                                                                                             |

Costs come from the model prices OpenCode knows, including cache and long-context prices. Without
them, the indicator and tips leave the amounts out.

## Install a local build

Run `mise run build cache-coach` from the repository root, then point the plugin entries in your
`opencode.json` and `cli.json` at the package directory, such as
`"package": "/path/to/opencode-plugins/packages/cache-coach"`, and restart OpenCode.

# opencode-forgekeeper

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that keeps coding sessions connected to their issues,
PRs/MRs, review feedback, and CI status. It supports GitHub and GitLab.

Session titles include the references you're working on. The prompt footer shows what needs
attention, and automatic summaries bring review feedback back into the relevant conversation.
A session can track several PRs/MRs across repositories.

![OpenCode session list with issue and MR references, a review notification, and a footer summarizing four MRs.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/main/packages/forgekeeper/images/session-review-notification.png)

Notification wording has changed since this capture.

## Installation

Requires OpenCode 2.2 or later, plus an authenticated [`gh`](https://cli.github.com/) for GitHub
or [`glab`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli) for GitLab. The CLI must be available on the
OpenCode server's `PATH`; only the CLI for your forge is required.

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-forgekeeper
```

OpenCode loads the server, terminal, and desktop parts automatically. Forgekeeper uses your
forge CLI's credentials and has none of its own. Without a forge CLI, session naming still works, and
`/forge-status` explains what's missing.

For self-managed hosts, configure `hosts` for GitLab hosts not named `gitlab.*`, or
`githubHosts` for GitHub Enterprise.

## Session targets

Ask the agent to work on an issue or PR/MR. Forgekeeper provides `set_session_target` and
instructions for the agent to keep the session's target up to date, including after creating
a PR/MR. Targets persist across reloads and need not match the checked-out branch.

For example, a session working on issue `#12` and MR `!45` gets a title prefix such as
`[#12, !45]`. Several targets produce `[!101, !102]`, or `[!101, !102, !103, +3]` for a larger set.
Your own title text is preserved.

Without an explicit target, naming follows the checked-out branch and its open PR/MR. Ask the
agent to return to branch-based naming when you want that behavior again. Default branches
get no branch-based prefix. Child sessions aren't renamed.

See the reference for [target rules](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#session-targets) and
[branch-based naming](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#branch-based-naming).

## PR/MR status

The footer shows CI, unresolved threads, conflicts, approvals, and running automated reviews.
Several targets show aggregate counts. Click the PR/MR number or pipeline to open it in the
browser, or another indicator to open the status dialog.

For example, this footer tracks four MRs, with one conflict and two already merged:

![Compact Forgekeeper footer reading four MRs, one conflict, and two merged.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/main/packages/forgekeeper/images/conflict-status-footer.png)

![Forgekeeper status dialog within an OpenCode session, showing pipeline results, unresolved threads, conflicts, and review requirements.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/main/packages/forgekeeper/images/review-and-ci-status.png)

| Command           | Action                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/forge-status`   | Show detailed status and refresh it. Aliases: `/mr-status`, `/pr-status`. |
| `/forge-open`     | Open the PR/MR in your browser. Aliases: `/mr-open`, `/pr-open`.          |
| `/forge-feedback` | Browse pending review feedback and PR/MR updates.                         |

In OpenCode Desktop, a pill above the composer shows the same status, and the commands
above open side panels for the status and the inbox. Server notices appear as toasts and
system notifications.

![OpenCode Desktop showing a merged MR, review-update summaries, and the Forgekeeper status panel.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/main/packages/forgekeeper/images/desktop-status.png)

Conflicts appear in both the composer pill and the status panel:

![OpenCode Desktop showing a PR with merge conflicts in the composer pill and Forgekeeper status panel.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/main/packages/forgekeeper/images/desktop-conflicts.png)

The OpenCode web app loads neither the terminal nor the desktop part, but it offers two
commands that answer in the conversation:

| Command         | Action                                                                                                              |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/forge-report` | Show the PR/MR status of the session.                                                                               |
| `/forge-inbox`  | List the session's pending updates. `ack <id>` or `ack all` acknowledges them, and `summarize <id>` summarizes one. |

Each answer is a short tool-free model turn that shows a report written from forge data.
Those apps don't display the text of messages that plugins add, so the model shows it.
The report stays out of the session's history.

Status normally refreshes every 2 minutes, or every 30 seconds during automated reviews and
while new review feedback settles.
Explicit PR/MR targets take precedence over title references and branch discovery. Issue
targets have no PR/MR status.

## Reviews and updates

Forgekeeper watches explicit PR/MR targets for human and automated review feedback, conflicts,
failed jobs, and merges. Recent top-level sessions can receive updates even if their tabs
aren't open. Branch-derived PRs/MRs get status but no review notifications.

New checkouts show status without collecting inbox updates. Open `/forge-feedback` and choose
**Enable feedback inbox** (Ctrl+S in the terminal) to start monitoring this checkout. Set
`inbox: true` to enable monitoring by default. Automation rules also opt in. A saved checkout
preference takes precedence, including one from before the upgrade.

**Mark all as read** (Ctrl+U in the terminal) clears the badge for the displayed updates and
keeps them in the inbox. An update arriving afterward stays unread. **Acknowledge** dismisses
an update locally. Neither action replies to or resolves a remote discussion.

To enable monitoring and summarize lifecycle updates automatically:

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-forgekeeper",
      "options": {
        "inbox": true,
        "delivery": { "lifecycle": "summary" }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Each delivery option accepts:

- `inbox` (default): retain the update without posting to the session.
- `passive`: queue a notice without starting a turn.
- `summary`: start a restricted summary turn after active work finishes. Review updates without
  comments use a passive notice instead.

Human and GitLab Duo feedback wait for a four-minute quiet period, with status polling every
30 seconds meanwhile, so an update arrives within about 5 minutes of the last comment. That's
before a typical 5-minute prompt cache expires. Monitoring records an initial baseline rather
than announcing existing feedback. Pending updates survive reloads and clear when acknowledged
or no longer relevant; merge updates remain until acknowledged.

On GitLab, a request for your review, including a repeated one, also becomes an update. It
links the author's replies since the previous request, including those in resolved threads. A
request is informational and never starts review automation.

Forgekeeper reports failed jobs but never retries or fixes them. For tracked stacks, it can
also propose retargeting dependents after a parent merges, but never retargets or rebases itself.

Optionally, `automation.rules` lets exact reviewers on exact projects, such as GitLab Duo, start
a coding turn that prepares fixes for their feedback. It runs only on PRs/MRs you wrote, or that
an account in the rule's `authors` wrote, in the one session that targets them, with the
checkout on the source branch. A rule can require models
you trust with code changes. The turn uses the session's instructions and permissions, and
leaves changes uncommitted. In `/forge-feedback`, **Act on feedback** (Ctrl+A) starts the same
turn on request, and **Retry feedback work** (Ctrl+T) retries one after you inspect it.

A `job-failed` rule investigates failed jobs on exact projects instead. Once a pipeline's
failures go quiet for four minutes, or the pipeline finishes, one turn reads the failed jobs'
logs and reports each failure's cause and a recommended fix, without changing anything. It runs
on PRs/MRs you wrote or review, or that an account in the rule's `authors` wrote, with the
checkout at the head commit the pipeline tested. See
[Investigate failed jobs](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#investigate-failed-jobs).

A session that tracks several PRs/MRs is on at most one of their branches. With
`"execution": "environment"` on a rule, a batch whose checkout is elsewhere runs through the
environment provider. The current local provider runs a linked session in a worktree at the
PR/MR's head commit, and the owning session gets a notice with its path.
Forgekeeper removes the worktrees it created once their PR/MR is over and nothing in them would
be lost. See
[Run automation in an execution environment](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#run-automation-in-an-execution-environment).

See [review detection and summaries](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#review-notifications),
[review requests](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#review-requests),
[monitoring eligibility](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#which-sessions-the-server-watches),
[stacked PRs/MRs](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#stacked-prsmrs), and
[preparing fixes](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#prepare-fixes-from-review-feedback) for details.

## Options

Set options in the object form of the plugin entry in `opencode.json`, as in the example above.
Only specify values you want to change. The terminal part has no separate options.

| Option                            | Default                       | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `status`                          | `true`                        | Set to `false` to keep only session targets and titles, without polling or notifications.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `hosts`                           | `["gitlab.com"]`              | Additional recognized GitLab hosts, besides hosts named `gitlab.*`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `githubHosts`                     | `["github.com"]`              | Recognized GitHub hosts, including Enterprise.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `pollSeconds`                     | `120`                         | Normal status polling interval.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `watch.humanReviews`              | `true`                        | Monitor human review feedback.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `watch.automatedReviews`          | `true`                        | Monitor GitLab Duo and GitHub Copilot review feedback.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `watch.reviewBots`                | `true`                        | Monitor configured review-bot accounts.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `watch.lifecycle`                 | `true`                        | Monitor conflicts, failed jobs, and merges.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `watch.reviewRequests`            | `true`                        | Monitor requests for your review on GitLab MRs, including repeated ones.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `reviewBots`                      | GitLab.com security reviewers | Exact bot usernames by host. Your list replaces the defaults.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `inbox`                           | `false`                       | Enable inbox monitoring for checkouts without a saved monitoring preference. Automation rules also enable it.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `delivery.reviews`                | `"inbox"`                     | Review delivery: `inbox`, `passive`, or `summary`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `delivery.lifecycle`              | `"inbox"`                     | Conflict, job-failure, and merge delivery.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `lifecycleExecution.parentMerged` | `{ "mode": "notify" }`        | Optionally prepare retarget proposals for tracked dependents.                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `automation.rules`                | No rules                      | Reviewers whose feedback starts a coding turn that prepares fixes, or projects whose failed jobs start an investigation, optionally limited to allowed models. Set `"execution": "environment"` to permit the configured environment provider when the owning checkout doesn't match. |
| `automation.modelGroups`          | No groups                     | Named lists of `provider/model` IDs that rules reference in `allowedModelGroup`.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

See the [configuration reference](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#options) for validation behavior and
[review-bot configuration](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#review-notifications) for account matching.

## Security and privacy

Monitoring reads forge data through your authenticated CLI. It doesn't modify the forge,
edit files, commit, push, reply to comments, or resolve discussions. Only an
[automation rule](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#prepare-fixes-from-review-feedback)
or **Act on feedback** starts a coding turn that edits files, with the session's permissions.
That turn sends reviewer text to the model as untrusted data, keeps it in the session's
history, and leaves changes uncommitted. A failed-job investigation sends job names and
links the same way, and the agent reads job logs with the session's tools.

Optional review summaries send review text to the session's model, isolated from conversation
history and ordinary tools. On GitLab, a restricted tool can read notes directly linked by
the announced comments, including private notes your credentials can access on the same host.
Review content is treated as untrusted data.

The inbox stores identifiers, links, and timestamps locally, not comment bodies or credentials.
Summary records temporarily retain review text in plugin storage. This is not OS-level
isolation, and the implementation has not received AppSec approval.

See the [security boundary](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#monitoring-security-boundary) and
[summary restrictions](https://github.com/pedropombeiro/opencode-plugins/blob/main/packages/forgekeeper/docs/reference.md#summary-turns) for limits and retention details.

- **From `opencode-forge-session-title` or Forgekeeper 1.x:** replace the package entry.

# opencode-homeassistant

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that sends agent status to [Home Assistant](https://www.home-assistant.io) via webhooks -- and optionally lets you respond to permission requests from HA.

Requires OpenCode 2.2 or later. For OpenCode 1, install the `opencode-v1` dist-tag
(`npm install opencode-homeassistant@opencode-v1`).

## Features

- Notifies Home Assistant when the OpenCode agent becomes busy, idle, waiting, or encounters an error
- Sends the hostname alongside the state, so you can identify which machine triggered the automation
- Tracks session duration -- `idle`, `waiting`, and `error` payloads include `durationMs` (time since the last `busy` event)
- Flushes pending webhooks when OpenCode exits, including a final `idle` update for active sessions
- Automatically cleans up sessions stuck in `busy` state after 10 minutes of no activity, checked every minute
- Per-state webhook routing -- send different states to different webhook IDs
- Multiple webhook targets -- send the same state to several Home Assistant instances
- Includes question choices in `waiting` payloads -- HA can render actionable notifications with the available options
- Remote permission response -- approve or deny agent permissions from HA (via entity polling)
- JSON payload, compatible with Home Assistant's webhook trigger out of the box

## States

| State     | OpenCode event                                                  | Description                             |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `busy`    | `session.execution.started`, repeated on `session.step.started` | Agent starts or continues processing    |
| `idle`    | `session.execution.succeeded`, `session.execution.interrupted`  | Agent finishes and is waiting for input |
| `waiting` | `permission.asked`                                              | Agent requests user permission          |
| `waiting` | `form.created`                                                  | Agent asks the user a question          |
| `error`   | `session.execution.failed`                                      | Session encounters an error             |

## Payload

The plugin sends a `POST` request with `Content-Type: application/json`:

```json
{
  "state": "idle",
  "hostname": "my-macbook",
  "project": "my-app",
  "sessionId": "01JFF...",
  "durationMs": 12345
}
```

| Field        | Description                                                                 |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `state`      | One of `busy`, `idle`, `waiting`, `error`                                   |
| `hostname`   | Machine hostname (`os.hostname()`)                                          |
| `project`    | Directory name of the current project                                       |
| `sessionId`  | OpenCode session ID (useful for correlating events)                         |
| `durationMs` | Milliseconds since the session became `busy` (omitted from `busy` payloads) |
| `waiting`    | Details about what the agent is waiting for (only on `waiting` payloads)    |

### `waiting` object

| Field       | Description                                                                      |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `reason`    | Either `permission` (agent needs approval) or `question` (agent asks a question) |
| `id`        | Permission ID or question request ID, used for remote replies                    |
| `type`      | Permission action, e.g. `shell`, `edit`, `webfetch` (only for `permission`)      |
| `title`     | Human-readable description of the request                                        |
| `pattern`   | The command or path pattern being requested (only for `permission`)              |
| `questions` | Array of question details with options (only for `question`)                     |

In a Home Assistant automation, access these values via `trigger.json.*`, e.g. `trigger.json.state`.

### Permission payload example

```json
{
  "state": "waiting",
  "hostname": "my-macbook",
  "project": "my-app",
  "sessionId": "ses_...",
  "durationMs": 4200,
  "waiting": {
    "reason": "permission",
    "id": "per_cd77d4766001...",
    "type": "shell",
    "title": "shell: mkdir test-folder",
    "pattern": ["mkdir test-folder"]
  }
}
```

### Question payload example

```json
{
  "state": "waiting",
  "hostname": "my-macbook",
  "project": "my-app",
  "sessionId": "ses_...",
  "durationMs": 5000,
  "waiting": {
    "reason": "question",
    "id": "frm_014e8b5fe001...",
    "title": "Choose framework",
    "questions": [
      {
        "header": "Choose framework",
        "question": "Which framework would you like to use?",
        "options": [
          { "label": "React", "value": "React", "description": "Component-based UI library" },
          { "label": "Vue", "value": "Vue", "description": "Progressive framework" }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Each question in the `questions` array has:

| Field      | Type       | Description                                             |
| ---------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `header`   | `string`   | Short label                                             |
| `question` | `string`   | Full question text                                      |
| `options`  | `array`    | Available choices (`label`, `value`, and `description`) |
| `multiple` | `boolean?` | Whether multiple selections are allowed                 |

## Installation

```bash
opencode plugin add opencode-homeassistant
```

This adds the plugin to your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["opencode-homeassistant"]
}
```

The package has a server entrypoint, which sends webhooks and polls Home Assistant, and a CLI
entrypoint, which OpenCode loads automatically. The CLI entrypoint only delivers question answers
from Home Assistant, because OpenCode 2 lets only CLI plugins reply to questions.

## Configuration

Create `~/.config/opencode/opencode-homeassistant.json`:

```json
{
  "webhookUrl": "https://your-home-assistant/api/webhook/your_webhook_id"
}
```

The config file path can be overridden with the `OPENCODE_HA_CONFIG_PATH` environment variable. See [webhook trigger documentation at Home Assistant](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/automation/trigger/#webhook-trigger).

You can also pass any of these settings as plugin options. Options take precedence over the config
file:

```json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-homeassistant",
      "options": { "webhookUrl": "https://ha.local/api/webhook/opencode_status" }
    }
  ]
}
```

If no webhook URLs are configured or the config file is missing, the plugin is disabled silently.
The plugin reads its configuration when it loads, so restart OpenCode after changing it.

### Debug log

The plugin writes nothing by default. To troubleshoot remote replies, enable the debug log:

```json
{
  "debug": true,
  "debugLogPath": "~/.local/state/opencode/homeassistant.log"
}
```

`debugLogPath` defaults to `~/.local/state/opencode/homeassistant.log`. At startup the plugin
records its resolved version and remote reply settings:

```text
started version=X.Y.Z, entity=input_text.opencode_permission_response, permissionTimeout=120s, remoteReplies=enabled
```

Each poll then records when it starts, which response it matched, and why it gave up.

### Per-state webhook routing

Use `webhookUrls` to send different states to different webhook IDs. A `default` key acts as a fallback for any state without its own entry:

```json
{
  "webhookUrls": {
    "busy": "https://ha.local/api/webhook/opencode_busy",
    "error": "https://ha.local/api/webhook/opencode_error",
    "default": "https://ha.local/api/webhook/opencode_general"
  }
}
```

With this config, `busy` and `error` events go to their own webhooks while `idle` and `waiting` fall back to the `default` webhook.

### Multiple webhook targets

Each entry in `webhookUrls` can be a single URL or an array, allowing you to notify multiple Home Assistant instances or trigger several automations at once:

```json
{
  "webhookUrls": {
    "default": [
      "https://ha-home.local/api/webhook/opencode_status",
      "https://ha-office.local/api/webhook/opencode_status"
    ],
    "error": "https://ha-home.local/api/webhook/opencode_errors"
  }
}
```

### Precedence

The plugin resolves webhook URLs in this order:

1. `webhookUrls[state]` -- exact match for the current state
2. `webhookUrls.default` -- fallback for unmatched states
3. `webhookUrl` -- legacy single-URL config (used when `webhookUrls` is absent)

### Remote permission response

The plugin can relay permission responses from Home Assistant back to OpenCode. When a `permission.asked` event fires, the plugin sends the webhook **and** starts polling an HA entity for a response. If the user answers the permission locally in the TUI, the poll aborts immediately.

To enable this, add the following to your config:

```json
{
  "webhookUrl": "https://ha.local/api/webhook/opencode_status",
  "haApiUrl": "https://ha.local/api",
  "haToken": "${HA_LONG_LIVED_TOKEN}",
  "permissionResponseEntity": "input_text.opencode_permission_response",
  "permissionTimeout": 120
}
```

| Field                      | Default                                   | Description                                               |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `haApiUrl`                 | _(required)_                              | Home Assistant REST API base URL                          |
| `haToken`                  | _(required)_                              | Long-lived access token (supports `${ENV_VAR}` expansion) |
| `permissionResponseEntity` | `input_text.opencode_permission_response` | Entity the plugin polls for the user's response           |
| `permissionTimeout`        | `120`                                     | Seconds to wait for a response before giving up           |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> `${ENV_VAR}` expansion reads the **opencode process environment**, not your interactive shell. Exporting the variable in `.zshrc` is not enough when opencode is launched from a GUI app, a launch agent, or any non-login context, and opencode does not read `.env` files. If the variable is missing, remote replies are silently skipped: the notification still arrives, but tapping it does nothing.
>
> A reliable option is a mise `[env]` entry, which does reach opencode:
>
> ```toml
> # ~/.config/mise/config.local.toml (machine-local, untracked)
> [env]
> HA_LONG_LIVED_TOKEN = "eyJhbGciOi..."
> ```
>
> To check what opencode actually sees, enable the [debug log](#debug-log) and answer a prompt. The plugin names the exact missing variable:
>
> ```text
> not polling because haToken references HA_LONG_LIVED_TOKEN,
> which is not set in the opencode process environment
> ```

**How it works:**

1. Plugin sends the `waiting` webhook (with `waiting.id` set to the permission ID or question request ID)
2. Plugin starts polling `permissionResponseEntity` every 2 seconds
3. HA automation shows an actionable notification; when the user taps an action, the automation sets the entity state (see formats below)
4. Plugin reads the response, clears the entity, and replies to OpenCode. Question answers go through the plugin's CLI entrypoint, so they need a connected OpenCode terminal interface.
5. If the user answers locally in the TUI instead, the plugin receives a `permission.replied`, `form.replied`, or `form.cancelled` event and stops polling immediately

Each pending request gets its own webhook and its own poll. When an agent asks for several permissions at once, you receive one notification per request and can answer them in any order. The session resumes only after every request has been answered, so make sure your automation includes the request ID in the response rather than assuming a single outstanding request.

**Response formats**

The entity value is disambiguated by splitting on `:`. A first segment of `question` marks a question response (3 segments); anything else is a permission response (2 segments).

| Kind       | Format                               | Example                 |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------- |
| Permission | `<permissionId>:<response>`          | `per_abc123:allow`      |
| Question   | `question:<requestId>:<optionIndex>` | `question:frm_xyz789:0` |

Valid permission responses: `allow`, `always`, `deny`.

`<optionIndex>` is a 0-based index into `questions[0].options` -- the same array sent in the `waiting` payload. An index is used rather than the label because labels may contain `:`, carry emoji, or exceed the `input_text` 255-character limit. If the index is out of range or unparsable, the plugin sends no reply rather than a malformed answer.

Notes and limits:

- Only `questions[0]` is answered. Multi-question requests are not supported.
- Exactly one option is sent, since iOS notification actions are single-tap. For `multiple: true` questions, the answer contains only that option.
- `custom: true` ("Type your own answer") is not representable, as HA builds buttons from `options` only.
- HA should clear the entity shortly after setting it (5 seconds is a good default) to stop stale values latching. The 2-second poll interval sits comfortably inside that window -- do not raise it much beyond 2s without widening the reset delay.

## Automation ideas

### Busy light / desk LED

Change the color of a smart bulb or LED strip based on agent state -- red for errors, yellow for waiting on input, green for busy, off when idle:

```yaml
automation:
  - alias: OpenCode busy light
    triggers:
      - trigger: webhook
        webhook_id: your_webhook_id
        allowed_methods:
          - POST
        local_only: false
    actions:
      - choose:
          - conditions: "{{ trigger.json.state == 'busy' }}"
            sequence:
              - action: light.turn_on
                target:
                  entity_id: light.desk_led
                data:
                  color_name: green
                  brightness: 128
          - conditions: "{{ trigger.json.state == 'waiting' }}"
            sequence:
              - action: light.turn_on
                target:
                  entity_id: light.desk_led
                data:
                  color_name: yellow
                  brightness: 200
          - conditions: "{{ trigger.json.state == 'error' }}"
            sequence:
              - action: light.turn_on
                target:
                  entity_id: light.desk_led
                data:
                  color_name: red
                  brightness: 255
          - conditions: "{{ trigger.json.state == 'idle' }}"
            sequence:
              - action: light.turn_off
                target:
                  entity_id: light.desk_led
```

### Track agent status as a template sensor (with multi-session support)

A [trigger-based template sensor](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/template/#trigger-based-template-sensors) gives you a rich entity with attributes and derived state logic. This version tracks multiple concurrent sessions -- one session going idle won't overwrite the state of another still-busy session:

```yaml
template:
  - trigger:
      - trigger: webhook
        webhook_id: your_webhook_id
        allowed_methods:
          - POST
        local_only: true
      - trigger: event
        event_type: timer.finished
        event_data:
          entity_id: timer.opencode_agent_state
    sensor:
      - name: OpenCode Agent Status
        unique_id: opencode_agent_status
        device_class: enum
        state: >
          {%- if trigger.platform == 'event' -%}
            idle
          {%- else -%}
            {%- set prev = this.attributes.get('sessions', {}) -%}
            {%- set sid = trigger.json.sessionId | default('unknown') -%}
            {%- set raw = trigger.json.state -%}
            {%- set was_busy_long = raw == 'idle'
                   and prev.get(sid, {}).get('state') == 'busy'
                   and (trigger.json.durationMs | default(0) | int) >= 10000 -%}
            {%- set effective = 'completed' if was_busy_long else raw -%}
            {%- set ns = namespace(states=[]) -%}
            {%- for k, v in prev.items() if k != sid and v.state != 'idle' -%}
              {%- set ns.states = ns.states + [v.state] -%}
            {%- endfor -%}
            {%- if effective != 'idle' -%}
              {%- set ns.states = ns.states + [effective] -%}
            {%- endif -%}
            {%- if ns.states | length == 0 -%}
              {{ effective }}
            {%- else -%}
              {%- set prio = {'error': 0, 'waiting': 1, 'busy': 2, 'completed': 3} -%}
              {%- set ns2 = namespace(best='idle', best_prio=99) -%}
              {%- for s in ns.states -%}
                {%- if prio.get(s, 50) < ns2.best_prio -%}
                  {%- set ns2.best = s -%}
                  {%- set ns2.best_prio = prio.get(s, 50) -%}
                {%- endif -%}
              {%- endfor -%}
              {{ ns2.best }}
            {%- endif -%}
          {%- endif -%}
        icon: >
          {%- set icons = {
            'busy': 'mdi:robot-outline',
            'waiting': 'mdi:robot-confused-outline',
            'error': 'mdi:robot-dead-outline',
            'completed': 'mdi:robot-happy-outline',
          } -%}
          {{ icons.get(this.state, 'mdi:robot-off-outline') }}
        attributes:
          sessions: >
            {%- if trigger.platform == 'event' -%}
              {}
            {%- else -%}
              {%- set prev = this.attributes.get('sessions', {}) -%}
              {%- set sid = trigger.json.sessionId | default('unknown') -%}
              {%- set raw = trigger.json.state -%}
              {%- set ns = namespace(sessions={}) -%}
              {%- for k, v in prev.items() if k != sid and v.state != 'idle' -%}
                {%- set ns.sessions = dict(ns.sessions, **{k: v}) -%}
              {%- endfor -%}
              {%- set was_busy_long = raw == 'idle'
                     and prev.get(sid, {}).get('state') == 'busy'
                     and (trigger.json.durationMs | default(0) | int) >= 10000 -%}
              {%- set effective = 'completed' if was_busy_long else raw -%}
              {%- if effective != 'idle' -%}
                {%- set entry = {
                  'state': effective,
                  'hostname': trigger.json.hostname | default(''),
                  'project': trigger.json.project | default(''),
                } -%}
                {%- set ns.sessions = dict(ns.sessions, **{sid: entry}) -%}
              {%- endif -%}
              {{ ns.sessions | to_json }}
            {%- endif -%}
          hostname: >
            {%- if trigger.platform == 'webhook' -%}
              {{ trigger.json.hostname }}
            {%- else -%}
              {{ this.attributes.get('hostname', '') }}
            {%- endif -%}
          project: >
            {%- if trigger.platform == 'webhook' -%}
              {{ trigger.json.project | default('') }}
            {%- else -%}
              {{ this.attributes.get('project', '') }}
            {%- endif -%}
          session_id: >
            {%- if trigger.platform == 'webhook' -%}
              {{ trigger.json.sessionId | default('') }}
            {%- else -%}
              {{ this.attributes.get('session_id', '') }}
            {%- endif -%}
          duration_ms: >
            {%- if trigger.platform == 'webhook' -%}
              {{ trigger.json.durationMs | default(none) }}
            {%- else -%}
              {{ this.attributes.get('duration_ms', none) }}
            {%- endif -%}
          waiting_reason: >
            {%- if trigger.platform == 'webhook' and trigger.json.waiting is defined -%}
              {{ trigger.json.waiting.reason | default(none) }}
            {%- elif trigger.platform == 'webhook' -%}
              {{ none }}
            {%- else -%}
              {{ this.attributes.get('waiting_reason', none) }}
            {%- endif -%}
          waiting_title: >
            {%- if trigger.platform == 'webhook' and trigger.json.waiting is defined -%}
              {{ trigger.json.waiting.title | default(none) }}
            {%- elif trigger.platform == 'webhook' -%}
              {{ none }}
            {%- else -%}
              {{ this.attributes.get('waiting_title', none) }}
            {%- endif -%}
          permission_id: >
            {%- if trigger.platform == 'webhook' and trigger.json.waiting is defined -%}
              {{ trigger.json.waiting.id | default(none) }}
            {%- elif trigger.platform == 'webhook' -%}
              {{ none }}
            {%- else -%}
              {{ this.attributes.get('permission_id', none) }}
            {%- endif -%}
          question_options: >
            {%- if trigger.platform == 'webhook' and trigger.json.waiting is defined
                  and trigger.json.waiting.questions is defined
                  and trigger.json.waiting.questions | length > 0
                  and trigger.json.waiting.questions[0].options is defined -%}
              {{ trigger.json.waiting.questions[0].options | to_json }}
            {%- elif trigger.platform == 'webhook' -%}
              []
            {%- else -%}
              {{ this.attributes.get('question_options', []) | to_json }}
            {%- endif -%}

timer:
  opencode_agent_state:
    name: OpenCode agent state auto-revert
    duration: '00:00:05'

automation:
  - alias: OpenCode agent state timer control
    mode: restart
    triggers:
      - trigger: state
        entity_id: sensor.opencode_agent_status
    actions:
      - if:
          - condition: state
            entity_id: sensor.opencode_agent_status
            state: [error, completed]
        then:
          - action: timer.start
            target:
              entity_id: timer.opencode_agent_state
        else:
          - action: timer.cancel
            target:
              entity_id: timer.opencode_agent_state
```

The aggregate state reflects the highest-priority active session (`error` > `waiting` > `busy` > `completed` > `idle`). The `sessions` attribute stores a dict of active sessions keyed by `sessionId`, each with `state`, `hostname`, and `project`.

The `completed` state is synthesized when the agent goes from `busy` → `idle` after at least 10 seconds -- a signal that a real task finished. The timer ensures transient states (`error`, `completed`) auto-revert to `idle` after 5 seconds. The `waiting_*` and `permission_id` attributes are cleared when a non-waiting webhook arrives, preventing stale values.

### Actionable mobile notification when waiting for input

Get a push notification with action buttons when the agent has been busy for a while (>30s) and then needs your input. This uses a **separate webhook** so it works independently of the sensor and correctly handles parallel sessions.

**Plugin config** -- route `waiting` payloads to both the sensor and the notification webhook:

```json
{
  "webhookUrls": {
    "default": "https://ha.local/api/webhook/opencode_agent_status",
    "waiting": [
      "https://ha.local/api/webhook/opencode_agent_status",
      "https://ha.local/api/webhook/opencode_agent_notify"
    ]
  }
}
```

Since `webhookUrls[state]` overrides `default` entirely, the `waiting` entry must include the sensor webhook too.

**HA automation** -- triggers on the notification webhook, reads all data from the payload:

```yaml
input_text:
  opencode_permission_response:
    name: OpenCode Permission Response
    initial: ''
    max: 255

automation:
  - alias: Notify when OpenCode needs input after long-running prompt
    mode: parallel
    max: 10
    triggers:
      - trigger: webhook
        webhook_id: opencode_agent_notify
        allowed_methods:
          - POST
        local_only: true
    conditions:
      - condition: template
        value_template: >
          {{ trigger.json.state == 'waiting'
             and (trigger.json.durationMs | default(0) | int) >= 30000 }}
    actions:
      - variables:
          waiting: '{{ trigger.json.waiting | default({}) }}'
          waiting_reason: "{{ waiting.reason | default('') }}"
          is_permission: "{{ waiting_reason == 'permission' }}"
          is_question: "{{ waiting_reason == 'question' }}"
          permission_id: "{{ waiting.id | default('') }}"
          question_options: >
            {%- if waiting.questions is defined
                  and waiting.questions | length > 0
                  and waiting.questions[0].options is defined -%}
              {{ waiting.questions[0].options }}
            {%- else -%}
              []
            {%- endif -%}
          action_approve: "{{ 'APPROVE_' ~ context.id }}"
          action_deny: "{{ 'DENY_' ~ context.id }}"
          action_always: "{{ 'ALWAYS_' ~ context.id }}"
      - variables:
          notification_message: >
            {{ trigger.json.project | default('unknown') }}
            on {{ trigger.json.hostname | default('unknown') }}
            {%- if waiting.title not in [none, ''] %}
            — {{ waiting.title }}
            {%- endif %}
          question_actions: >
            {%- set opts = question_options if question_options is list else [] -%}
            {%- set ns = namespace(actions=[]) -%}
            {%- for opt in opts[:10] -%}
              {%- set ns.actions = ns.actions + [{"action": "OPT_" ~ loop.index0 ~ "_" ~ context.id, "title": opt.label}] -%}
            {%- endfor -%}
            {{ ns.actions }}
      - choose:
          - alias: Permission notification
            conditions: '{{ is_permission }}'
            sequence:
              - action: notify.mobile_app_your_phone
                data:
                  title: opencode is waiting for input
                  message: '{{ notification_message }}'
                  data:
                    push:
                      interruption-level: time-sensitive
                    actions:
                      - action: '{{ action_approve }}'
                        title: Approve
                      - action: '{{ action_deny }}'
                        title: Deny
                        destructive: true
                      - action: '{{ action_always }}'
                        title: Always Allow
              - wait_for_trigger:
                  - trigger: event
                    event_type: mobile_app_notification_action
                    event_data:
                      action: '{{ action_approve }}'
                  - trigger: event
                    event_type: mobile_app_notification_action
                    event_data:
                      action: '{{ action_deny }}'
                  - trigger: event
                    event_type: mobile_app_notification_action
                    event_data:
                      action: '{{ action_always }}'
                timeout: '00:02:00'
                continue_on_timeout: true
              - choose:
                  - alias: Approve
                    conditions: '{{ wait.trigger is defined and wait.trigger.event.data.action == action_approve }}'
                    sequence:
                      - action: input_text.set_value
                        target:
                          entity_id: input_text.opencode_permission_response
                        data:
                          value: '{{ permission_id }}:allow'
                  - alias: Always Allow
                    conditions: '{{ wait.trigger is defined and wait.trigger.event.data.action == action_always }}'
                    sequence:
                      - action: input_text.set_value
                        target:
                          entity_id: input_text.opencode_permission_response
                        data:
                          value: '{{ permission_id }}:always'
                  - alias: Deny
                    conditions: '{{ wait.trigger is defined and wait.trigger.event.data.action == action_deny }}'
                    sequence:
                      - action: input_text.set_value
                        target:
                          entity_id: input_text.opencode_permission_response
                        data:
                          value: '{{ permission_id }}:deny'
          - alias: Question notification with options
            conditions: '{{ is_question and question_actions | length > 0 }}'
            sequence:
              - action: notify.mobile_app_your_phone
                data:
                  title: opencode is waiting for input
                  message: '{{ notification_message }}'
                  data:
                    push:
                      interruption-level: time-sensitive
                    actions: '{{ question_actions }}'
        default:
          - action: notify.mobile_app_your_phone
            data:
              title: opencode is waiting for input
              message: '{{ notification_message }}'
              data:
                push:
                  interruption-level: time-sensitive
```

Key design choices:

- **Dedicated webhook** (`opencode_agent_notify`) -- the automation triggers directly from the webhook payload, not from sensor state changes. This avoids race conditions when multiple sessions are active and ensures `durationMs` is accurate per-session.
- **`mode: parallel`** -- multiple concurrent sessions can each have their own notification in-flight.
- **`durationMs >= 30000`** -- uses the plugin's per-session busy timer instead of HA's `last_changed`, which can be inaccurate when sessions overlap.
- **Permission reply** -- tapping Approve/Deny writes to `input_text.opencode_permission_response` using the format `<permissionId>:<response>`, which the plugin polls for.
- **Question actions** -- dynamically builds notification buttons from the question's options (up to 10, the iOS limit). Tapping one writes `question:<requestId>:<optionIndex>` to the same entity; the plugin resolves the index back to the option label and replies to OpenCode.

### Session duration tracking

Log how long each agent interaction took. The `durationMs` field is included in `idle`, `waiting`, and `error` payloads, measuring the time since the session last became `busy`:

```yaml
automation:
  - alias: OpenCode session duration
    triggers:
      - trigger: webhook
        webhook_id: your_webhook_id
        allowed_methods:
          - POST
        local_only: false
    conditions:
      - condition: template
        value_template: '{{ trigger.json.durationMs is defined }}'
    actions:
      - action: input_number.set_value
        target:
          entity_id: input_number.opencode_last_duration_seconds
        data:
          value: '{{ (trigger.json.durationMs / 1000) | round(1) }}'
```
